title: fix: restrict thread archiving to creators and admins
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes members being able to archive threads created by someone else when they have general write access.

## User Impact

Members can archive and restore only threads they created; admins retain access across creators. Assigned ownership alone no longer grants archive or restore access, including for existing sessions after an upgrade. This is the requested policy change; the multi-user guide documents admin recovery when the creator is unavailable or lacks usable profile attribution. Other collaboration actions, assigned-owner stop controls, and solo gateways retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enforce creator/admin authority at the shared Gateway authorization boundary for single and batch patches, including checks after asynchronous work. Align the UI and agent controls so an unauthorized self-archive cannot report success before being rejected. The conflict resolution preserves main's newer session-assignment support.

## Evidence

- [CI run 36762379844](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36762379844) passed on `c8704d67e8f1c49c85b98115cf37aa19f3a100bb`; `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review are green.
- Verified the original CI failures before editing: the positive UI restore fixture omitted creator authority, and the assembled Gateway fixture still expected assigned-owner archiving. Subsequent CI exposed MCP and deferred self-archive fixtures with the same stale authority assumptions. The fixtures now exercise creator authority, assignment-independent archive rights, and late revocation/replacement rejection with persisted-state assertions.
- 251 distinct focused tests passed across 15 files over the local validation runs: Gateway single/batch authorization and lifecycle, assembled/deferred controls, real MCP HTTP and dispatch, assignment/stop controls, and UI permissions. The final shared-fixture validation passed all 39 tests in its two consumer files (164 seconds).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main` and the follow-up `--staged` checks passed: formatting, production and test types, i18n, lint, dead-export scans, and the selected repository guards.
- Independent conflict review, Codex autoreview, fresh fixture/documentation reviews, and the [ClawSweeper review of the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160932#issuecomment-5883311816) found no actionable issues.
- The unrelated cron lint failure is fixed upstream by [743c2ceb72e7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/743c2ceb72e7d1372845ea6f834bb82993fc9e0e), included by the rebase; the affected cron file passes lint locally.
- Six Chromium flows passed on the original implementation: member/other, member/own, and admin/other, each for archive and restore. The retained screenshots use the built Control UI with a deterministic mocked Gateway; they are not a deployed-server smoke test.

Before: a member can archive another creator's thread.

![Before: member can archive another creator's thread](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cb3f996-2786-4e34-a26b-2554963cb5cf)

After: the same action is disabled with a creator/admin explanation.

![After: archive requires the creator or an admin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf91c1e4-5e32-4ad4-9179-2b1198d7bf6a)
